clue.text: A costing process he claims not to know

indicators.note: to process material is to work it over, so the letters of these two words are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone sceptical of a bureaucratic costing exercise says he knows nothing about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'process' tells you to rearrange A COSTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who holds that God's existence is unknowable claims no knowledge either way.

clue.text: Bill sees programmed note retrieved from computer

parts.note: ACC, short for account, is a bill

indicators.note: programmed suggests something set up afresh, so the letters of sees are rearranged

parts.note: D is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: Someone named Bill watches a coded musical note pulled up on a computer screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name but is an account; 'programmed' rearranges the letters of 'sees' into ESSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Data opened or fetched from a computer has been got at, in computing jargon.

clue.text: Keep going on about how to use an embrocation

explanation.surface: Advice on applying liniment doubles as a complaint about someone who nags.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep harping on a sore point is the idiom; literally, liniment is massaged into the skin.

clue.text: A group of investigators put in charge is sharp

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: A team of detectives given command proves acerbic.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the plain-clothes detective branch of British police.
explanation.definitionFit: Sour or tart in taste or manner, like a sharp remark or vinegar.

clue.text: Working habits provoking ridicule in Nazi security forces

indicators.note: in places the word for ridicule within the letters for the Nazi forces

parts.note: the SS was the Nazi paramilitary security organisation
to ridicule is to mock

explanation.surface: Uniforms that draw scorn are worn by Hitler's security troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provoking' is a link. 'Working habits' reads as routines, but habits here are garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose overgarments worn while doing messy work are a kind of work clothing.

clue.text: One of the Lords Spiritual with conservative views?

definitions.text: One of the Lords Spiritual with conservative views?

parts.words: One of the Lords Spiritual with conservative views?
parts.note: a bishop in the House of Lords favouring traditional, ritual-rich Anglican worship

explanation.surface: A traditionalist bishop sitting in the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lords Spiritual are the Church of England bishops who sit in the House of Lords; 'conservative' points to the ritualist wing of Anglicanism.
explanation.definitionFit: An Anglican favouring elaborate ceremony and sacramental tradition, as a conservative bishop might.

clue.text: Two former Prime Ministers possess the right to symbolise the house

indicators.note: the two leaders hold the letter for right within their names, as if possessing it

parts.note: Edward Heath and Alec Douglas-Home were both British Prime Ministers
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Two ex-premiers own the right to stand for domestic life.
explanation.walkthrough: Heath and (Douglas-)Home were British Prime Ministers in the 1960s and 70s; R goes into HEATH to give HEARTH.
explanation.definitionFit: The fireside and dwelling together are a stock phrase standing for domestic life.

clue.text: Preservation society which has the confidence of the people

parts.note: something belonging to a whole people or country is national
confidence in someone is trust

explanation.surface: A heritage charity enjoys public trust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which has' links the pieces. The National Trust is the British charity that looks after historic houses and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: The British charity that conserves historic buildings and landscapes.

clue.text: Transatlantic girl with mineral wealth in abundance

parts.note: gal is an American informal word for a girl
ore is rock rich in valuable minerals

explanation.surface: An American woman has plenty of mining riches.
explanation.definitionFit: Plentiful, aplenty, used after a noun.

clue.text: Show I acted in by order

indicators.note: putting letters into a new order means rearranging the three words before it

explanation.surface: An actor says they were cast in a play by command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by order' signals rearranging I ACTED IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To point out or signal something is to display it.

clue.text: Conventional group of people

explanation.surface: A conformist social circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Fixed or established, as in set phrases; also a social circle, the jet set.

clue.text: Conditions in North America

explanation.surface: Circumstances on the American continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Conditions are situations someone is in; the US is often simply called the country of fifty of them.

clue.text: In the Channel Islands senate initially gets no one to back cut

parts.note: CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands

indicators.note: initially picks only the opening letter of the word senate
going back means the words for no and one are read right to left

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Channel Islands parliament won't support anyone, it gets cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to back' turns NO + I into ION; 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgical cut is a slit made in the body.

clue.text: Heiress whose heart is filled with anger

indicators.note: the central letters of the heiress word hold the run that gives the answer

explanation.surface: A rich young woman seethes inside with rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrath, fury: a literary word for rage.

clue.text: Downfall of a rotter in a legal action

indicators.note: in places the word for rotter inside the word for a legal action

parts.note: a case is a lawsuit
a cad is a rotter, a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A scoundrel's ruin comes through a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downfall' read literally is water falling in stages.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterfall tumbling down in stages, literally a falling down of water.

clue.text: A measurement of twelve inches at the stern

parts.note: FT is the abbreviation for foot, which is twelve inches

explanation.surface: A one-foot measurement at the back of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Towards the rear of a ship, in nautical language.

clue.text: Hard cheese! It's in the Mendips

explanation.surface: Bad luck, says someone, about a place in Somerset's hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard cheese!' is British slang for bad luck, but here it simply names a hard cheese. The Mendips are hills in Somerset, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm English cheese; also a Somerset village and gorge in the Mendip Hills.

clue.text: Aggressive merchandising technique which makes it all too easy to buy!

definitions.text: Aggressive merchandising technique which makes it all too easy to buy!

parts.words: Aggressive merchandising technique which makes it all too easy to buy!
parts.note: a pushy sales method; ironically, the phrase literally suggests a difficult trade, yet it makes buying effortless

explanation.surface: A pushy sales pitch makes purchasing irresistible.
explanation.definitionFit: High-pressure salesmanship that pushes customers into buying.

clue.text: Remove from the House of Hades

parts.note: Dis is another name for the underworld or its ruler
a lodge is a small house

explanation.surface: Being thrown out of the underworld's residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the' and 'of' are links; Dis is the Roman name for the underworld, put first.
explanation.definitionFit: To shift or force out of a fixed position.

clue.text: Divided as to where Tom Sawyer might be found

definitions.text: as to where Tom Sawyer might be found

explanation.surface: Split over where to find a famous fictional boy.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Sawyer is a character created by Mark Twain, so he is found in Twain's writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Split into two parts, in old usage; also literally inside the works of Twain, Tom Sawyer's author.

clue.text: Taking on a child is a choice of the present era

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era
an option is a choice

explanation.surface: Becoming a parent by law is a modern option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is a' and 'of' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Legally becoming the parent of someone else's offspring.

clue.text: He carries cases of wine with little hesitation

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
er is the small sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A man carries crates of wine without hesitating much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cases' looks like cases of wine; it belongs to the definition, luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: A luggage carrier at a station or hotel.

clue.text: I get Sid to throw out imbeciles

indicators.note: throwing out suggests scrambling, so the letters of the two words after I are rearranged

explanation.surface: I get Sid to eject some fools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throw out' rearranges SID TO into DIOTS, after I; 'get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Fools or simpletons; an old insult for stupid people.

clue.text: Following breakdown sister takes the examination again

indicators.note: a breakdown breaks the word sister apart so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: After a nervous collapse, a sister retakes her exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' is a link; 'breakdown' rearranges SISTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Sits a test a second time after failing it.

clue.text: Make hay, Edward

explanation.surface: Someone called Edward turning hay in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: To spread out grass for drying; also a short form of the name Edward.

clue.text: Not a good outlook in the opinion of theneedy

explanation.surface: The poor take a dim view of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theneedy' is 'the needy' run together in print; the second reading is the opinion held by the poor.
explanation.definitionFit: A dim or bleak prospect; also, literally, the opinion of those in poverty.

clue.text: Plug recommendation to defer retirement

explanation.surface: Advice to delay going to bed, or to block a hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' means going to bed, not giving up work.
explanation.definitionFit: To block a hole; also advice to remain awake late instead of going to bed.

clue.text: If you've got it you're not in the dark

definitions.text: If you've got it you're not in the dark

parts.words: If you've got it you're not in the dark
parts.note: literally a household lamp keeps you out of darkness, punning on being in the know

explanation.surface: Being informed means you're not ignorant.
explanation.definitionFit: Illumination from bulbs powered by mains supply.
